To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The dopamine uptake system in the brain is able to recognize dopamine as a substrate, but it is also able to accept other conformationally restricted derivatives of dopamine as substrates.

(1) dopamine and noradrenaline are taken up by the synaptosomal uptake system in their gauche rotamer conformations; (2) dopamine and nor-adrenaline are taken-up in the same conformation by the uptake site in the synaptosome; and (3) the uptake site is conformationally different in dopamine and nor-adrenalin uptake.
the conformational preference of the dopamine uptake site in the brain is the gauche rotamer, and this preference is different in the 5-HT uptake site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conformational aspects of catecholamines and their uptake.
the conformational requirements for uptake of catecholamines and indoleamines by the synaptosomal membrane.
the conformational requirements of dopamine and 3,4-dimethoxyphenylethylamine for their interaction with the uptake sites of these compounds in rat brain synaoptosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dopamine uptake system is able to accept a dopamine analogue with a gauche relation of the catechole ring and the amino group, but the 5-HT uptake system is not.
the conformation of the substrate is of importance for the interaction with both uptake systems.
the dopamine uptake system is able to accommodate the dopamine molecule with a gauche conformation, and that the conformational requirement for 5-HT uptake is more strict.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformation of the catecholic moiety is a crucial factor in the interaction of dopamine with its uptake system.
the conformational requirements for dopamine uptake are more stringent than those for 5-HT uptake.

dopamine uptake sites are conformationally flexible and accept substrates in different conformational states, whereas 5-HT uptake sites are conformed to accept only one conformational state of the substrate.

we have shown for the first time that the 3,4-dimethoxyphenethylamine moiety is a potent and selective inhibitor of 5-HT reuptake.
the dopamine transporter is a flexible protein that can accept the substrate as a gauche rotamer, and the dopamine transporter is conformationally different from the serotonin transporter.
